title: Exchange of product samples
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces, with strictly positive coordinate weights summing to $1$, and let $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. For any function $F$ of two product outcomes, the expectation over independent $x,y$ drawn from $P$ of $F$ evaluated on the pair that uses $x_i,y_i$ on $S$ and $y_i,x_i$ off $S$ equals the expectation of $F(x,y)$ over independent $x,y$ drawn from $P$.
hypotheses_covered: A finite product of n coordinate probability spaces
S is a subset of the coordinate indices
F is a real-valued function of two product outcomes
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $S\subseteq[n]$, and $F:\Omega\times\Omega\to\mathbb R$, where $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$. For independent $X,Y\sim P$, let $X\mathbin{\star_S}Y$ keep $X_i$ on $S$ and $Y_i$ elsewhere; then $\mathbb E F(X\mathbin{\star_S}Y,Y\mathbin{\star_S}X)=\mathbb EF(X,Y)$.
